subject: Runtime dependency carveout request: structured-output & tool-call failures affecting Checkout API
messages:
From: Alice Monroe <alice@fastretail.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Structured output tool-call failures impacting Checkout API

Hi Stephanie,

We started seeing an uptick in errors from the Checkout content flow this morning. Calls that require structured output (order JSON schema) are intermittently returning 500/timeout errors when the filter/tool-call step runs, and in several cases the fallback returned an unstructured string. This is impacting our checkout conversion—we've observed a ~3% drop in success for orders between 08:45-09:20 PT and elevated latency on subsequent retries.

I've attached a short logs extract (FastRetail_incident_logs_20270620.txt) with request ids and timestamps. Our SRE (ops@fastretail.com) would like to understand whether this qualifies for an SLA carve-out versus an availability incident. We need clarity on:
- What component failed (content filter vs tool call latency vs model structured-output generator)
- Whether this is a persistent condition you can remediate or an allowed exception under the contract
- If a carve-out is granted, effective window and any credits to expect

Can you review and loop in the right folks? We're on a Black Friday-like week for campaign launches, so the timing is tight.

Thanks,
Alice Monroe
Head of Engineering, FastRetail

Forwarding FastRetail incident. Summary: external reports intermittent 500s/timeouts originating during the content-filter -> tool-call -> structured-output path. They included request ids; attaching a proposed carveout draft (proposed_carveout_draft.docx) for initial review.

Immediate asks:
1) Triage and root-cause quick note (karthik) — is this filter lag, tool-call queuing, or model structured-output generation mismatch?
2) Legal/business: recommend provisional carveout window (start/end/timezone) + preliminary credit calc (percent of monthly usage or pro-rata uptime credit).
3) Ops: propose mitigations we can push immediately (circuit-breaker to non-filtered path, rate limit backoff, temporary pin to older model variant).

My proposed customer-facing wording (draft):
- We acknowledge the incident and are proposing a provisional carve-out for structured-output failures tied to the filter/toolchain that caused degraded output or timeouts between 2027-06-20T15:30:00Z and 2027-06-20T16:10:00Z. During this period the service degraded due to an external dependency (third-party content classifier) and the platform's automated fallback behaved inconsistently. We propose a one-time credit equal to 10% of June usage for affected routes, contingent on sign-off.

Please respond with technical read and approval to present to the customer.

—Stephanie
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed_carveout_draft.docx (document, 28KB)
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Fwd: Structured output tool-call failures impacting Checkout API

Stephanie — quick technical notes after an initial pass through the logs:
- The request ids show the pattern: content filter requests spiked and a downstream moderation classifier timed out (p95 latency ~2.7s when target was 200ms). The tool-call queue on the filter worker filled for a ~3 minute window and caused backpressure into the structured-output generator, leading to timeouts and occasional fallback to the generic text generator.
- Root cause candidate: an upstream classifier regression (third-party model) that increased compute per call under a specific payload distribution; our runtime observed queue saturation before the fallback rate limiter could engage.

Immediate mitigations we can apply (non-cust impactful, rollable within 45m):
1) Enable aggressive circuit-breaker on filter path for FastRetail routes — force fallback to validated non-filtered structured output path (losing moderation gating but preserving JSON schema).
2) Temporarily pin to stable model variant for structured-output generation to avoid fallback diversity.
3) Adjust worker autoscaling to pre-warm additional filter replicas for the affected cluster — will reduce p95 latency.

Carveout recs:
- Window proposal: 2027-06-20T15:33:00Z -> 2027-06-20T16:12:00Z (matches logs).
- Credit proposal: pro-rata uptime credit for the affected routes equal to 12% of June billable usage for those endpoints (technical justification attached in internal doc).

I'll open RED-8421 to track the permanent fix and link to this thread. Please confirm if we want me to apply mitigation 1 immediately; it will temporarily relax content filtering for their checkout route.

—Karthik
Director, Runtime Reliability
From: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Structured output tool-call failures impacting Checkout API

Thanks for the fast triage. Approve provisional carveout and the immediate mitigations Karthik outlined under these conditions:
- Mitigation 1 (circuit-breaker to structured-output fallback) may be applied once Customer Ops signs off on the temporary relaxation of filtering for checkout traffic.
- Credit decision: provisional credit up to 12% of June usage for affected checkout routes, to be finalized after legal review and after we confirm the exact affected request set.

Action items:
1) Stephanie — present the provisional carveout wording to FastRetail and ask for Ops sign-off on the reduced-moderation fallback.
2) Laura — engage Legal to draft the carveout amendment (DocuSign) and confirm final credit calc methodology.
3) Karthik — if customer approves, implement mitigation 1 and monitor for 24h; keep RED-8421 updated and attach the incident logs.

Let's keep the window narrow and put a 48-hour review cap on the carveout. If symptoms persist we escalate to a longer remediation plus follow-on credit.

—Markus
VP, Customer Engineering
